name: quenching
description: OKF-centric knowledge-base aligner for the Claude Code surface of any repository. It acts on three fronts — the docs/ OKF bundle, the native specs/ spec-driven workspace, and the .claude/ command surface — and every front has exactly one align: /docs:align, /specs:align, /skill:align, with the root /align conducting all three in dependency order on a single confirmation and looping across them until nothing changes anywhere. Each align is probe-first, so a conformant front costs a couple of tool calls and stops. Around them: inserts knowledge into the right home, curates a fixed A–Z glossary, drains project memory into docs, refactors CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md into thin pointers, imports external sources as OKF docs, builds and maintains the mkdocs site over the documentation/ home, mints and measures commands, subagents and hooks, and drives the spec cycle (create → develop → execute → conclude, with continue routing between them, plus triage and status) with the bundle as its knowledge substrate — entirely native, no external CLI, no delta, no separate spec store: a spec writes its durable rules straight into docs/standards/, isolated on a real git branch whose per-task commits it records, and three deterministic stdlib Python tools (okf-validate.py, specs.py, skills.py) give the commands their rails behind a uniform --json and strict exit codes. Twenty-four commands, one file per entry point — the path is the identity, no skills/ tree and no wrapper — each keeping default invocation under /docs:*, /specs:*, /skill:* and the root /align. Every repository that adopts it looks the same.
